patterns.title: Opposite-End Two Pointers
patterns.summary: Converge left and right pointers towards the center to find pairs, partition elements, or reverse collections in linear time.
trigger_cues: Array or string is sorted (or can be sorted in O(N log N))
Target is to find a pair or triplet summing to a value
Partitioning elements or checking palindromes in-place
invariant_rules: Pointers satisfy left < right at each step
All candidate solutions outside [left, right] have already been evaluated and eliminated
If current_sum < target, incrementing left strictly increases the sum (assuming sorted non-decreasing)
common_pitfalls: Applying to an unsorted array without sorting first
Off-by-one index with right = size vs right = size - 1
Omitting pointer advance in branch causing an infinite loop

patterns.title: Dynamic Sliding Window
patterns.summary: Expand a contiguous window with a right pointer while contracting with a left pointer to satisfy a state invariant.
trigger_cues: Subarray or substring contiguous range requirement
Longest/shortest range satisfying condition (e.g., at most K distinct elements)
Running sum or character frequency within a range
invariant_rules: Window [left, right] contains elements that maintain or approach the target constraint
Right pointer expands the candidate range by 1 on each outer loop
Left pointer contracts the window until the invariant is restored
common_pitfalls: Contracting window before evaluating or updating state counters
Re-scanning window from scratch rather than updating incremental frequency diffs
Failing to clean up map keys when frequency drops to 0

patterns.title: Fast & Slow Pointers (Floyd's Cycle Finding)
patterns.summary: Move two pointers at different speeds (1x and 2x) across a linked list or cyclical sequence to detect cycles or locate midpoints in O(1) space.
trigger_cues: Detect if a linked list or sequence contains a cycle
Find the midpoint of a linked list in a single pass
Find the entry node of a circular loop
invariant_rules: In a cycle of length L, the relative distance between fast and slow decreases by 1 node per iteration
Slow and fast will meet in at most L iterations once slow enters the cycle
When slow and fast meet, resetting slow to head and moving both at 1x finds the cycle entrance
common_pitfalls: Null pointer dereference: forgetting to check both fast and fast->next before accessing fast->next->next
Misidentifying midpoint for even-length lists (depending on slow/fast initialization)
Overcomplicating with auxiliary hash sets when O(1) space is achievable

patterns.title: Monotonic Stack
patterns.summary: Maintain elements in a strictly increasing or decreasing order on a stack to resolve nearest greater/smaller element queries in linear time.
trigger_cues: Find the next greater or smaller element for each index in an array
Find largest rectangle in histogram or trapping rain water bounds
invariant_rules: The stack always contains indices whose values satisfy the monotonic invariant (e.g. descending)
Incoming element pops all stack items that violate the invariant, resolving their queries
Each element is pushed once and popped at most once, giving amortized O(N) time
common_pitfalls: Storing values in the stack instead of indices when distances or indices are required
Using strict < versus <= leading to duplicate values improperly grouped
Assuming O(N^2) complexity because of nested while loop: each element enters and leaves once

patterns.title: State-Space Backtracking
patterns.summary: Explore state candidates recursively and systematically undo state modifications (backtrack) upon encountering invalid states.
trigger_cues: Generate all permutations, combinations, or partitions
Constrained search spaces (e.g. Sudoku, Word Search, N-Queens)
Find all valid decision paths through a graph or tree
invariant_rules: State before branching is identically restored after the recursive call returns
Base condition correctly records a completed leaf snapshot into results
Pruning condition terminates branches early if partial state cannot lead to valid solution
common_pitfalls: Forgetting to undo state modification (pop_back or reset flag), corrupting neighboring branches
Missing base return condition leading to recursion stack overflow
Failing to sort input array before handling duplicate candidates

decision_matrix.scenario: Frequent random access and key-based lookup

candidates.space_overhead: High (buckets, hashes, and linked collision nodes)
candidates.best_when: Unordered key lookup where average O(1) performance is required
candidates.avoid_when: Sorted order iteration or strict worst-case latency bounds are mandatory

candidates.best_when: Keys must stay ordered, or predecessor/successor range queries are needed
candidates.avoid_when: Only raw equality lookups are needed and average O(1) is preferred

candidates.best_when: Dataset is immutable or bulk-loaded once and queried heavily
candidates.avoid_when: Frequent runtime insertions and deletions occur

decision_matrix.scenario: Continuous retrieval and streaming updates of minimum or maximum element

candidates.time_complexity: O(1) find extremum, O(log N) push/pop
candidates.best_when: Only need top priority element (min or max) without searching arbitrary keys
candidates.avoid_when: Need to search, delete, or update arbitrary middle elements

candidates.time_complexity: O(log N) min/max, O(log N) push/pop
candidates.best_when: Need extremum access AND arbitrary deletions / range lookups simultaneously
candidates.avoid_when: Only priority access is needed (unnecessary overhead)

candidates.best_when: Extremum is queried extremely rarely compared to writes
candidates.avoid_when: Streaming queries or frequent top-element consumption

decision_matrix.scenario: Frequent insertions and removals at the front or middle

candidates.time_complexity: O(1) insert/remove given node pointer, O(N) to seek by index
candidates.best_when: LRU caches, constant-time splice and node relocation with existing iterators
candidates.avoid_when: Need random access by index (O(N) traversal penalty)

candidates.time_complexity: O(1) push/pop at both front and back, O(1) indexed lookup
candidates.best_when: Sliding window buffers, job queues, double-ended queues
candidates.avoid_when: Frequent insertions in the middle of the collection

candidates.time_complexity: O(N) insert/remove at front/middle, O(1) amortized append
candidates.best_when: Appends and random index access dominate over prepends
candidates.avoid_when: Prepend or frequent middle deletions (requires shifting elements)

decision_matrix.scenario: Range queries [L, R], predecessor, successor, and sorted traversal

candidates.time_complexity: O(log N + K) range scan, O(log N) insert/delete
candidates.best_when: Dynamic dataset with real-time modifications requiring sorted bounds
candidates.avoid_when: Data is completely static or known upfront

candidates.time_complexity: O(log N + K) range scan, O(N) insert/delete
candidates.best_when: Static or read-only datasets with excellent CPU cache locality

candidates.time_complexity: O(N) full table scan for any range query
candidates.avoid_when: Any range query or sorted iteration is required
